question.text: What do the colors and shapes of regulation, warning, destination and service signs tell you?

answer.text: Sign shape and color announce their job: regulation signs are normally white rectangles with black or red markings, warnings yellow diamonds with black, destinations green with white, and services blue with white.

teaching.text: Read the color and shape first: white rectangles regulate, yellow diamonds warn, green shows destinations, and blue shows services. Remember: shape and color tell.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Sign shape and color announce their job: regulation signs are normally white rectangles with black or red markings, warnings yellow diamonds with black, destinations green with white, and services blue with white.

question.text: What does a stop sign require, and where exactly do you stop?

answer.text: The red-and-white stop sign demands a full stop with right-of-way yielded, halting before the stop line, else the crosswalk, else the nearest point with a clear view into the intersection.

teaching.text: A stop sign always means a full stop, at the stop line first, then the crosswalk, then the nearest clear view. Remember: line, crosswalk, sight point.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The red-and-white stop sign demands a full stop with right-of-way yielded, halting before the stop line, else the crosswalk, else the nearest point with a clear view into the intersection.

question.text: What does a yield sign require?

answer.text: The red-and-white yield sign demands slowing, traffic checks and readiness to stop, a full stop whenever conditions require, and yielded right-of-way.

teaching.text: A yield sign means slow, check and be ready, stopping fully only when conditions require it. Remember: slow, check, maybe stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The red-and-white yield sign demands slowing, traffic checks and readiness to stop, a full stop whenever conditions require, and yielded right-of-way.

question.text: How do stop and yield signs differ, and what do they share?

answer.text: Stop always halts fully while yield halts only when traffic demands, yet both yield right-of-way and both pick the stop line, crosswalk or sight point in the same order.

teaching.text: Stop always halts; yield halts only when traffic demands, and both use the same stopping points in the same order. Remember: stop always, yield sometimes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stop always halts fully while yield halts only when traffic demands, yet both yield right-of-way and both pick the stop line, crosswalk or sight point in the same order.

question.text: What do the other regulation signs cover, and what does a red circle with a slash mean?

answer.text: Other regulation signs rule direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and special cases, with a red circle-and-slash banning the pictured action or vehicle and rectangular white signs flagging special rules.

teaching.text: The red circle with a slash bans whatever action or vehicle it shows, and white rectangles flag special rules. Remember: circle-slash means no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Other regulation signs rule direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and special cases, with a red circle-and-slash banning the pictured action or vehicle and rectangular white signs flagging special rules.

question.text: What do yellow-and-black warning signs do, and what does an advisory speed sign add?

answer.text: Yellow-and-black warnings mark hazards and special rules, sometimes paired with a yellow-and-black advisory speed urging slower travel.

teaching.text: Yellow-and-black signs warn of hazards, and an advisory speed with them urges you to slow down. Remember: yellow warns, slow advised.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yellow-and-black warnings mark hazards and special rules, sometimes paired with a yellow-and-black advisory speed urging slower travel.

question.text: What do orange-and-black work signs mean, and what must drivers do in work zones?

answer.text: Orange-and-black work signs mark active work with possible flag control and work limits as low as twenty-five, and drivers slow through every work zone and obey every flag signal with or without a posted limit.

teaching.text: Orange-and-black means active work: slow through every work zone and obey every flag signal, posted limit or not. Remember: orange means work, slow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Orange-and-black work signs mark active work with possible flag control and work limits as low as twenty-five, and drivers slow through every work zone and obey every flag signal with or without a posted limit.

question.text: How do yellow warning signs differ from orange work signs?

answer.text: Yellow warnings advise caution with advisory speeds while orange work signs command slowdowns with enforceable limits and flag obedience, advice versus orders.

teaching.text: Yellow advises, orange orders: advisory speeds versus enforceable work-zone limits and flaggers. Remember: advice versus orders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yellow warnings advise caution with advisory speeds while orange work signs command slowdowns with enforceable limits and flag obedience, advice versus orders.

question.text: What do green-and-white destination signs and route markers show?

answer.text: Green-and-white destination signs give direction and distance, while varied route markers name interstate, United States, state or county roads by shape, in sample order state, United States, interstate, for map planning and en-route tracking.

teaching.text: Green-and-white signs give direction and distance, and route markers name the kind of road by their shape. Remember: green guides, shapes name.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Green-and-white destination signs give direction and distance, while varied route markers name interstate, United States, state or county roads by shape, in sample order state, United States, interstate, for map planning and en-route tracking.

question.text: What do blue-and-white service signs point to?

answer.text: Blue-and-white service signs point to rest areas, fuel, camping and medical help.

teaching.text: Blue-and-white signs point you to rest areas, fuel, camping and medical help. Remember: blue means services.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Blue-and-white service signs point to rest areas, fuel, camping and medical help.

question.text: How are signal lights arranged, and what do you do at a dead signal?

answer.text: Signals normally stack red, yellow and green top-to-bottom or left-to-right, appearing lone, flashing, round or arrowed, and dead or broken signals force a stop-sign stop followed by right-of-way rules unless an officer directs otherwise.

teaching.text: Signals usually run red, yellow, green from top to bottom or left to right, and a dark signal means stop as at a stop sign. Remember: dark signal, stop sign.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signals normally stack red, yellow and green top-to-bottom or left-to-right, appearing lone, flashing, round or arrowed, and dead or broken signals force a stop-sign stop followed by right-of-way rules unless an officer directs otherwise.

question.text: What does a steady red light mean, and when may you turn on red?

answer.text: Steady red means stop until green, or arrow-only movement on a green arrow when clear; right on red and one-way-to-one-way left on red are allowed after a full stop with yielding, except where signs, signals or markings forbid, anywhere unposted in the city, and right on red never for a school bus carrying students.

teaching.text: Steady red means stop; right on red is allowed after a full stop and yielding, except where forbidden, in the city unless posted, or for a school bus with students. Remember: stop, then maybe turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Steady red means stop until green, or arrow-only movement on a green arrow when clear; right on red and one-way-to-one-way left on red are allowed after a full stop with yielding, except where signs, signals or markings forbid, anywhere unposted in the city, and right on red never for a school bus carrying students.

question.text: What do a flashing red light and a red arrow mean?

answer.text: Flashing red equals a stop sign with stop, yield and safe-go, while a red arrow bans all movement its way until it clears, including any turn on red.

teaching.text: Flashing red works exactly like a stop sign, while a red arrow allows no movement its way, not even a turn on red. Remember: flashing red equals stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing red equals a stop sign with stop, yield and safe-go, while a red arrow bans all movement its way until it clears, including any turn on red.

question.text: How do a steady red, a red arrow, and a city red differ for turning?

answer.text: Steady red allows right turns and one-way-to-one-way lefts after stopping, a red arrow allows nothing, and city reds allow nothing unposted, three reds with three answers.

teaching.text: Three reds, three answers: steady red allows the listed turns after stopping, a red arrow allows nothing, and city reds allow nothing unposted. Remember: three reds, three answers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Steady red allows right turns and one-way-to-one-way lefts after stopping, a red arrow allows nothing, and city reds allow nothing unposted, three reds with three answers.

question.text: What do steady yellow, flashing yellow and a yellow arrow mean?

answer.text: Steady yellow warns of imminent red with stopping preparation, flashing yellow orders caution, and a yellow arrow ends green-arrow protection with stopping preparation for intending turners.

teaching.text: Steady yellow means red is coming, flashing yellow means caution, and a yellow arrow ends the protected turn. Remember: yellow means prepare.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Steady yellow warns of imminent red with stopping preparation, flashing yellow orders caution, and a yellow arrow ends green-arrow protection with stopping preparation for intending turners.

question.text: How do flashing red and flashing yellow differ, and how do steady yellow and a yellow arrow differ?

answer.text: Flashing red copies the stop sign while flashing yellow only urges caution, and steady yellow warns of red while a yellow arrow ends protected turning.

teaching.text: Flashing red copies the stop sign while flashing yellow only urges caution. Remember: copy stop versus caution.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing red copies the stop sign while flashing yellow only urges caution, and steady yellow warns of red while a yellow arrow ends protected turning.

question.text: What do a steady green light and a green arrow allow?

answer.text: Steady green and green arrows both permit movement while still yielding right-of-way as the law requires.

teaching.text: Green, steady or arrow, lets you move, but you still yield as the law requires. Remember: green goes, still yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Steady green and green arrows both permit movement while still yielding right-of-way as the law requires.

question.text: What do overhead lane lights mean?

answer.text: Overhead lane lights ban the lane on a steady red X, order exit on a steady yellow X, restrict to left turns on a flashing yellow X, and open the lane on a green arrow.

teaching.text: Lane lights overhead: red X closed, steady yellow X leave, flashing yellow X left turns only, green arrow open. Remember: red X, lane closed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Overhead lane lights ban the lane on a steady red X, order exit on a steady yellow X, restrict to left turns on a flashing yellow X, and open the lane on a green arrow.

question.text: What jobs does road paint do, and what does an edge line mark?

answer.text: Road paint divides lanes, gates passing and lane changes, assigns turn lanes and stop points; edge lines mark the shoulder boundary that crossing breaks except by official order or sign, and an inward-angling edge line warns of narrowing.

teaching.text: Paint divides lanes, controls passing and turn lanes, and an edge line marks the shoulder you may not cross unless an order or a sign allows it. Remember: paint sorts the road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Road paint divides lanes, gates passing and lane changes, assigns turn lanes and stop points; edge lines mark the shoulder boundary that crossing breaks except by official order or sign, and an inward-angling edge line warns of narrowing.

question.text: What do white and yellow lines separate, and what does a single broken line allow?

answer.text: White divides same-direction lanes and yellow divides opposing flows in solid or broken pairs, and one broken line allows passing or lane changes when safe and non-interfering.

teaching.text: White separates lanes going your way, yellow separates opposing traffic, and a single broken line lets you pass when safe. Remember: white same, yellow opposite.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White divides same-direction lanes and yellow divides opposing flows in solid or broken pairs, and one broken line allows passing or lane changes when safe and non-interfering.

question.text: When a solid line runs beside a broken line, what may each side do?

answer.text: Beside a solid-and-broken pair, the solid side bans passing and crossing except for a left into a driveway, while the broken side passes when safe and non-interfering.

teaching.text: With a solid and a broken line together, your side decides: solid means stay, broken means pass when safe. Remember: solid side stays.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Beside a solid-and-broken pair, the solid side bans passing and crossing except for a left into a driveway, while the broken side passes when safe and non-interfering.

question.text: What do double solid lines and a single solid line allow?

answer.text: Double solid lines ban passing, lane changes and crossing except to turn left entering or leaving the road or to U-turn, while a single solid line allows passing and changes only when obstructions or traffic force it.

teaching.text: Double solid lines allow crossing only for a left turn into or out of the road or a U-turn, and a single solid line allows only forced moves. Remember: double solid, lefts only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Double solid lines ban passing, lane changes and crossing except to turn left entering or leaving the road or to U-turn, while a single solid line allows passing and changes only when obstructions or traffic force it.

question.text: How do the four center-line patterns rank from least to most strict?

answer.text: Broken center lines invite passing, solid-and-broken splits permission by side, double solid forbids everything but lefts, and single solid allows only forced moves, a four-step strictness ladder.

teaching.text: Four patterns, four permissions: broken invites passing, solid-and-broken depends on your side, double solid allows only lefts and U-turns, single solid allows only forced moves. Remember: four-step line ladder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Broken center lines invite passing, solid-and-broken splits permission by side, double solid forbids everything but lefts, and single solid allows only forced moves, a four-step strictness ladder.

question.text: When do stop lines and crosswalk lines require a stop?

answer.text: Signed or signaled intersections may paint a white stop line or parallel crosswalk lines, stopping falls before whichever exists only when a device, officer or yielding pedestrian, skater or scooter user demands it, and set-back single lines shelter truck turning room.

teaching.text: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk when a device, officer or yielding pedestrian, skater or scooter user calls for it. Remember: stop when demanded.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signed or signaled intersections may paint a white stop line or parallel crosswalk lines, stopping falls before whichever exists only when a device, officer or yielding pedestrian, skater or scooter user demands it, and set-back single lines shelter truck turning room.

question.text: Does a painted stop line or crosswalk by itself force you to stop?

answer.text: Stop lines and crosswalks trigger stops only when a device, officer or yielding user demands, so bare paint alone never forces a halt.

teaching.text: Paint alone never forces a halt; the stop comes from a device, an officer or someone you must yield to. Remember: paint alone never halts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stop lines and crosswalks trigger stops only when a device, officer or yielding user demands, so bare paint alone never forces a halt.

question.text: What do lane arrows tell you, and when must you choose your lane?

answer.text: Lane arrows dictate lane use, such as right-only from the right lane and straight-only from the left, with lane choice settled before the solid separator.

teaching.text: Lane arrows assign your movement, so pick your lane before the solid separator begins. Remember: arrows assign lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Lane arrows dictate lane use, such as right-only from the right lane and straight-only from the left, with lane choice settled before the solid separator.

question.text: Who may use a diamond lane, and when may other drivers enter it?

answer.text: Diamond lanes reserve for buses, high-occupancy vehicles, bicycles and posted specials during posted times, with city broken-white gaps admitting non-carpool right turns at the next corner, all to speed the highest-value traffic.

teaching.text: Diamond lanes are reserved for buses, carpools, bicycles and posted vehicles during posted times. Remember: diamonds for buses, carpools.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Diamond lanes reserve for buses, high-occupancy vehicles, bicycles and posted specials during posted times, with city broken-white gaps admitting non-carpool right turns at the next corner, all to speed the highest-value traffic.

question.text: Whose directions override signs, signals and markings?

answer.text: Officer directions beat every sign, signal and marking, including stop-on-green and go-on-red orders, from police, fire police, work flaggers, crossing persons and school bus drivers.

teaching.text: Directions from police, fire police, flaggers, crossing persons and school bus drivers outrank every sign, signal and marking. Remember: officers outrank everything.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Officer directions beat every sign, signal and marking, including stop-on-green and go-on-red orders, from police, fire police, work flaggers, crossing persons and school bus drivers.

question.text: Who may use a diamond lane besides posted vehicles, and what overrides the diamonds?

answer.text: Diamond lanes exclude general traffic except posted compliers and corner-turning entrants, while officer orders override every marking including the diamonds themselves.

teaching.text: Only posted users and corner-turning entrants may use diamond lanes, and an officer's order still overrides them. Remember: corner turners, officers override.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Diamond lanes exclude general traffic except posted compliers and corner-turning entrants, while officer orders override every marking including the diamonds themselves.

question.text: What do a dead signal and a flashing red have in common?

answer.text: Dead signals degrade to stop-sign behavior with right-of-way rules, the same fallback a flashing red gives, while officers can override both.

teaching.text: A dark signal falls back to stop-sign behavior, just like a flashing red, and an officer can override both. Remember: dark equals stop sign.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Dead signals degrade to stop-sign behavior with right-of-way rules, the same fallback a flashing red gives, while officers can override both.
